hook: Surface activity reshaped Earth's deep interior 3.4 billion years ago, according to University of Portsmouth researchers.

sections.voiceover: Surface activity reshaped Earth's deep interior 3.4 billion years ago, according to University of Portsmouth researchers.

sections.voiceover: Scientists from the University of Portsmouth examined tiny mineral inclusions trapped in ancient zircon grains. How did this surface material reach the mantle?
sections.visual_cue: Laboratory setting at the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility showing scientists working at a console.
sections.sfx_cue: Sound of rapid, rhythmic digital data processing.

sections.voiceover: But scientists used the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility's ID21 beamline to reveal this hidden process.
sections.visual_cue: Graphic showing sulfur valence speciation data on a screen.

sections.voiceover: Nature Geoscience, a scientific journal, details how oxygen-weathered rocks were dragged into the Earth's interior. Hugo Moreira and his team traced this cycle back 3.4 billion years.
sections.visual_cue: Animated diagram showing surface material subducting deep into Earth's mantle.

sections.voiceover: This recycling of oxidized surface material into the Earth's interior began 3.4 billion years ago.
